messages:
nora: hi team, first-week onboarding hiccup. built the runtime from source in the dev container but runtime dies at first gpu convolution with cuDNN errors when running the integration smoke. build succeeded and linker resolved cuDNN, but runtime fails at startup. any ideas?

nora: runtime output snippet:

nora: ```
$ ./bazel-bin/runtime/examples/conv_smoke --input=test.bin
[INFO] initialising gpu backends
E cuDNN: CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
E runtime::gpu: failed to create cudnn handle: CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  cudnnCreate failed: 3
Aborted (core dumped)
```

nora: ldd on the binary shows it links to libcudnn.so.8 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8, but `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8 | grep CUDNN_MAJOR` prints 7 in the container (so it's v7 headers vs v8 runtime?).

mika: welcome! that mismatch between headers used at build time and the actual cuDNN runtime in the image is a classic onboarding trap. which dev image tag are you using? some older images ship cuDNN7 while our bazel toolchain expects cuDNN8.

nora: using `redwood/dev-container:cuda12.2-base` from quickstart. I built with the workspace toolchain set to `cuda12.2-cudnn8` (default on main).

tiago: confirm the header used at compile-time: `grep -R \"CUDNN_MAJOR\" bazel-out -n || true` or check the include path that Bazel used. But easiest fix: use the matching dev image that includes cuDNN8 (`redwood/dev-container:cuda12.2-cudnn8`) or mount the host's /usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib into the container.

nora: I tried `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64 ./bazel-bin/runtime/examples/conv_smoke` and got the same error. `nvidia-smi` shows host driver ok.

mika: LD_LIBRARY_PATH won't help if the container's libcudnn.so is older; you need the correct libcudnn.so.8 present. If you have the cudnn debs locally, you can copy the libcudnn.so.8 into the container's /usr/lib or prefer switching to the cudnn8 dev image. For onboarding, we recommend switching images to avoid weird local installs.

tiago: also check if the process can't allocate GPU memory due to cgroup limits in the dev workspace; cuDNN sometimes reports NOT_INITIALIZED when GPU init fails. Try running `cuda-smi` or a simple `device_query` binary to verify the process can talk to the GPU.

nora: ran device_query from CUDA samples in the container and it reports devices fine. I think it's the cuDNN version mismatch.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-578: "onboard: cuDNN version mismatch in dev container causing CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED" and assigned to infra oncall. Tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-578 :ticket:

devex: FYI - we have a `redwood/dev-container:cuda12.2-cudnn8` image for branches that need cuDNN8; quickstart will be updated. For a hotfix you can `docker pull` that tag and rebuild inside it. We'll also add a pre-flight script to the quickstart that detects header/runtime cuDNN mismatch.

nora: switched to cuda12.2-cudnn8 image and rebuilt. conv_smoke now runs and prints expected outputs. thanks! i'll link INF-578 if infra wants to update the default dev container. :thumbsup:

mika: awesome — welcome aboard and thanks for filing that repro. small follow-up PR to the quickstart to suggest the cudnn8 image for runtime dev would help future new hires.

nora: opening the PR now, adding a short note about verifying cuDNN header/runtime versions and the device_query sanity check. thanks for the quick help :wave:
